config.title: Design systems

intro.title: Design systems
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, reusable button component to understand the basics of a design system. You will learn how to create a consistent UI element by defining its visual properties and behavior in one place. The core programming concept used is component-based architecture, which allows you to encapsulate and reuse code. You will work with JavaScript, React components, and CSS styling to implement this. By the end, you'll see how design systems help maintain consistency and efficiency across a frontend application.
intro.usecase: Design systems are foundational in large-scale applications like enterprise dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and SaaS products. For example, a dashboard might use a consistent set of buttons, modals, and data tables defined in the system to ensure uniformity across admin panels and user interfaces. Developers rely on these systems to efficiently build and maintain complex features like filterable data grids or multi-step forms while enforcing brand and accessibility standards. This pattern is critical for teams to scale UI development, reduce inconsistencies, and streamline collaboration between designers and engineers.

objectives: Construct a reusable Button component with consistent styling and props.
Apply a color palette and typography scale to style components.
Configure a spacing system using CSS custom properties for layout consistency.
Integrate a Button component into a user interface to handle user interactions.
Manipulate component variants (e.g., primary, secondary) through props.
Initialize a basic design token system to centralize visual values.
Render a simple component library page demonstrating multiple styled components.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React and the useState hook into your file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules for use
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the DesignSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DesignSystem that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called DesignSystem that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the DesignSystem component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A DesignSystem component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is named DesignSystem and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named exactly 'DesignSystem' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a functional component called DesignSystem that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize design tokens state
steps.instruction: Inside your DesignSystem component, use useState to create a state variable called 'tokens' with initial values for primaryColor, secondaryColor, baseSpacing, and fontFamily.
steps.hint: Use useState to declare a state variable. Provide an object with the four properties as the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state with object initial value
const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: 'Alex', age: 25 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'tokens' state variable ready to store design system values.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an object containing primaryColor, secondaryColor, baseSpacing, and fontFamily properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've initialized state, but check that your object includes all four properties: primaryColor, secondaryColor, baseSpacing, and fontFamily.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tokens state isn't properly initialized. Use useState with an object containing the four design token properties.

steps.title: Define token update handler
steps.instruction: Inside your DesignSystem component, create a function named updateToken that takes tokenName and newValue as parameters and updates the tokens state accordingly.
steps.hint: You can use the setTokens function from useState to update the state. Remember to preserve existing tokens while updating the specific one.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an updateToken function that can modify individual design tokens while keeping the rest unchanged.
successCriteria: The updateToken function is defined with tokenName and newValue parameters and properly updates the tokens state using setTokens.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly updates the specific token while preserving others.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateToken function isn't defined correctly. Check that it takes two parameters and uses setTokens to update state.

steps.title: Return component structure
steps.instruction: Return a main container div with the className 'design-system' from your DesignSystem component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX div element that has the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX container element that will hold the design system demo content.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className 'design-system'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div with exactly className='design-system'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className 'design-system'.

steps.title: Add design tokens display section
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a div with className 'tokens-display' that shows the current token values from the tokens state.
steps.hint: Create a div element with the className attribute set to 'tokens-display'. Inside this div, you can display each token value using curly braces, like {tokens.primaryColor}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying state values in a div

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'tokens-display' div is added to the component structure, showing the current primaryColor, fontSize, and spacing values from the tokens state.
successCriteria: The component returns a div with className 'tokens-display' that contains the token values from the tokens state object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it has className 'tokens-display' and shows the token values from the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tokens display section is missing or incorrect. Add a div with className 'tokens-display' that displays the token values.

steps.title: Add token controls section
steps.instruction: Add a new div with className 'token-controls' inside the main component wrapper, after the tokens display section.
steps.hint: You can add a new div element with the specified class name directly inside the main wrapper div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component structure now includes a new div with className 'token-controls' placed after the tokens display section comment.
successCriteria: A div element with className 'token-controls' is added inside the main wrapper div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a div element with the exact className 'token-controls' inside the main wrapper div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The token controls section wasn't added correctly. You need to add a div with className 'token-controls' inside the main wrapper div.

steps.title: Wire token controls to update handler
steps.instruction: Add an onChange handler to each input field that calls updateToken with the appropriate token name and the input's current value.
steps.hint: Use the onChange event on each input to call updateToken with two arguments: the token name (like 'primaryColor') and event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each input field will have an onChange handler that calls updateToken with the correct token name and the input's value, enabling interactive updates to the design tokens.
successCriteria: All three input fields have onChange handlers that call updateToken with the appropriate token name and event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some onChange handlers, but not all inputs are wired correctly. Make sure each input calls updateToken with the correct token name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input fields are not properly connected to the update handler. Each input needs an onChange handler that calls updateToken with the token name and the input's value.

steps.title: Add component demo section
steps.instruction: Add a new section element with a heading 'Component Demo' and a div with className 'component-demo' inside your component's return statement.
steps.hint: Add this section after the existing token controls section. Use the <section> tag for the section and <h2> for the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a new section to demonstrate components

Component Demo

{/* Components will go here */}
steps.expectedOutcome: A new section with heading 'Component Demo' and an empty div with className 'component-demo' appears after the token controls section.
successCriteria: The component includes a new <section> element with an <h2> heading 'Component Demo' and a <div> with className 'component-demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the section with heading and the div with className 'component-demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component demo section wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added a new section element with heading and div after the token controls.

steps.title: Apply design tokens to demo components
steps.instruction: Apply inline styles to the button and card components in the demo section using the current token values from state.
steps.hint: Use the style attribute with JavaScript objects that reference tokens.primaryColor, tokens.fontSize, and tokens.spacing.
steps.analogousExample:
// Applying inline styles with state values
<button style={{ backgroundColor: colorState, fontSize: sizeState }}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button and card components in the demo section should visually reflect the current design token values (color, font size, spacing) when you adjust them with the controls.
successCriteria: The button has inline styles using tokens.primaryColor for background, tokens.fontSize for font size, and tokens.spacing for margin. The card has inline styles using tokens.primaryColor for border color, tokens.spacing for padding and margin, and tokens.fontSize for the heading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styles, but make sure all three tokens (primaryColor, fontSize, spacing) are applied to both the button and card components as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The demo components don't yet use the design tokens for styling. Apply inline styles to the button and card using the token values from state.
